normalized.description: Ordregiver udbyder en totalentreprisekontrakt vedrørende projektering, opførelse og idriftsættelse af Løvbak-kernes Vandværk nord for Herning. Vandværk placeres på matrikel nr. 1r, Gullestrup, Herning Jorder. Det nye vandværk skal have en produktionskapacitet på 3 millioner m³/år, med mulighed for udvidelse til 4,5 millioner m³/år efter 2040. Hovedformålet med det nye vandværk er at sikre fremtidens produktion af drikkevand og højne Herning Vands forsyningssikkerhed. Desuden ønskes muligheden for at kunne udvide vandværket på sigt og sikre fleksibilitet i forhold til den fremtidige efterspørgsel på rent vand. Det nye vandværk ved Løvbakkerne omfatter blandt andet byggemodning, vandværksbygning, el- og maskinan-læg, håndtering af skyllevand og overfladevand, vejanlæg og udenomsarealer på vandværksgrundens matrikel. Visionen hos ordregiver er, at vandværket opføres på en måde, hvor det integreres harmonisk og naturligt i land-skabet. Samtidig ønskes placeringen tæt på forsyningens boringer og eksisterende læringsmiljøer udnyttet, så vandværkets udearealer bliver centrum for et nyt læringsrum med fokus på bæredygtig vandforvaltning, grund-vandsbeskyttelse og formidling om vand. Det nye vandværk forventes færdigt medio 2029.

normalized.description: QLEO, a mission proposed as candidate mission in the frame of the Call for Earth Explorer 12 mission ideas, aims to provide tropospheric profiles of water vapour at the global scale with a high vertical resolution and a low bias, to close an important observational gap for climate and atmospheric research. The mission uses a spaceborne Differential Absorption LiDAR (DIAL) that enables precise measurements of atmospheric water vapor and trace gases. Following the evaluation, the Advisory Committee for Earth Observation strongly commended QLEO for its high scientific interest, while further developments need to be undertaken to mature some critical technologies. Spaceborne DIAL systems rely on advanced laser technology capable of emitting multiple wavelengths with high energy and stability, ensuring accurate detection of atmospheric gas concentrations over large scales. For DIAL-systems, these wavelengths have to be matched to characteristic absorption lines that usually do not overlap with the emission wavelength of the laser source. For QLEO wavelengths around 935 nm have been identified. Recent advancements in the field of spaceborne high energy (>400 mJ) single-frequency laser sources at 1064 nm wavelength and improvements in frequency converters based on optical-parametric oscillators make multi-wavelength systems in other spectral range more feasible for space deployment. Based on these promising results, existing laser technology concepts for frequency converters can be further enhanced to define suitable architectures for multi-pulse generation around 935 nm, and to increase the maximum achievable multipulse repetition rate. The technology developed can be used in Earth Observation LiDAR payloads with multi-wavelength laser transmitters around 935 nm but also with some modifications at different wavelengths, with the potential of improving conversion efficiency and advancing pulse overlap strategies. The objective of the activity is to enhance the maturity of critical elements and to demonstrate the overall functions and performance of the laser sub-system through the development of a dedicated breadboard with testing. The activity will cover the following key tasks: Evaluate and compare suitable architecture for conversion from 1064 nm to 935 nm wavelength. Design, build and test a representative model for the non-linear crystal mount. Design, manufacture and test a full breadboard, which includes pump source, frequency conversion and emission at multiple wavelengths around 935 nm. Assess through an analytical model the system performance and durability under various energy and environmental conditions (i.e.: radiation, Laser-Induced Damage Threshold - LIDT, etc.). Define a qualification plan for opto-mechanical packages. Prepare a development plan for an Engineering Model.The tenderer will be expected to have access to a suitable pump laser source to be used as an input signal for the frequency conversion at 935 nm.
